title: (Push) is an isomorphism for $F/E$ finite
statement:
For finite extensions $E\le F$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside $\Qlb$ and every morphism of schemes
$f\colon X\to Y$, the comparison (Push) ([def-sfb-derived-push-hom]) for the coefficient change
$E\to F$ ([def-sfb-subfield-coefficient-map]; flat by [lem-sfb-subfield-flat]),

$$
T^Y_{E,F}\circ Rf_*\longrightarrow Rf_*\circ T^X_{E,F},
$$

is an isomorphism of functors on the unbounded derived category $D(\Mod_{E_X})$.

proof.text: Put $d=[F:E]$. Choose an $\mathcal O_E$-basis $b_1,\ldots,b_d$ of $\mathcal O_F$ by [lem-sfb-local-field-integral-basis]. By [det-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients-finite-free], the same basis gives $E_W^{\oplus d}\cong F_W$ for $W=X,Y$, compatible with inverse image along $f$. Write $q_i^W:F_W\to E_W$ for the inverse coordinates. In particular the basis section $b_i^Y$ maps to $b_i^X$ under the coefficient pullback. The scalar maps here are precisely those of [def-sfb-subfield-coefficient-map].

Write $U_W=D(\operatorname{Res}_{E_W\to F_W})$ and $T_W=T^W_{E,F}$. Restriction is exact and extension is right exact by [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]; extension is also left exact by [lem-sfb-subfield-flat], hence exact. Thus $T_W\cong D(\operatorname{Ext})$, termwise extension on the unbounded derived category, by the exact-functor clause of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]; from step 5 on this identification is the isomorphism $\psi$ fixed there, which changes nothing below since only some natural isomorphism is used here. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-free-scalar-coordinates] to step 1: its maps are $s\otimes m\mapsto(q_i^W(s)m)_i$ and $(m_i)\mapsto\sum_i b_i^W\otimes m_i$. Derive this natural isomorphism using [lem-sfb-exact-derived-natural-iso], identifying the derived composite with $U_WT_W$ using [lem-sfb-exact-derived-composition]. This gives $U_WT_WL\cong L^{\oplus d}$ naturally in $L$. These formulas hold termwise on complexes and commute with differentials. Under this identification the $i$th injection is $j_i^W(L):m\mapsto b_i^W\otimes m$; no assertion about tensor sheaf sections being sectionwise tensor products is needed.

Put $G=Rf_*^E$ and $H=Rf_*^F$. The adjunction $Lf_E^*\dashv G$ is part of [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-limits] to the finite discrete diagram of $d$ copies of $K$: $G(K^{\oplus d})\to(GK)^{\oplus d}$, with components $G(\pi_i)$, is an isomorphism. Here products are biproducts because the derived categories are additive [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The inverse is the canonical finite-sum map $a_K:(GK)^{\oplus d}\to G(K^{\oplus d})$ with components $G(\iota_i)$: composing with $G(\pi_j)$ gives the identity for $i=j$ and zero otherwise. Indeed $G$ preserves zero objects, hence zero morphisms, since it preserves the empty product. Only finite products, not arbitrary coproducts or properness of $f$, enter.

The functor $U_Y$ reflects isomorphisms. To see this, restriction in [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars] is exact and unchanged on underlying objects and maps. It reflects module isomorphisms: if $u$ has underlying inverse $v$, the equation $u(r v(y))=r y=u(v(r y))$ gives linearity of $v$. Exactness identifies $H^n(U_YL)$ with $\operatorname{Res}(H^nL)$, since kernels, images and their quotient defining cohomology are preserved. If $U_Y(u)$ is invertible, every restricted $H^n(u)$ is invertible, so every $H^n(u)$ is invertible by the preceding inverse calculation. The criterion [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology], applied in the category of $F_Y$-modules, then makes $u$ invertible.

Let $e:U_YH\xrightarrow{\sim}GU_X$ be [def-sfb-derived-comap-lower-star-iso], and let $c_K:T_YGK\to HT_XK$ be (Push) [def-sfb-derived-push-hom]. Write $\eta^W$ for the unit of $T_W\dashv U_W$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars]. Substituting the unit--comparison--counit composite of [def-sfb-mate-push-hom] and cancelling the unit and counit by the adjunction triangle identity gives
$$e_{T_XK}\,U_Y(c_K)\,\eta^Y_{GK}=G(\eta^X_K).$$
This determines the image of the tensor with $1$, not yet those with the other basis elements. It remains to identify $\eta^W$ with the termwise unit $u_M:M\to\operatorname{Res}(F_W\otimes_{E_W}M)$, $m\mapsto1\otimes m$. Let $\lambda:\mathrm{id}\to U_WD(\operatorname{Ext})$ be the localization of $u$ (natural on $D(\Mod_{E_W})$, since it is natural for maps of complexes), and $\psi:T_W\to D(\operatorname{Ext})$ its transpose under $T_W\dashv U_W$, so $U_W(\psi)\,\eta^W=\lambda$. Apply [lem-sfb-exact-right-adjoint-kflat-representative] with $\mathcal C=\Mod_{E_W}$, $\mathcal D=\Mod_{F_W}$, $E=\operatorname{Ext}\dashv U=\operatorname{Res}$ and the chosen adjunction $T_W\dashv U_W$: $\Mod_{E_W}$ is Grothendieck, closed symmetric monoidal with additive tensor and functorial flat resolutions by [lem-sfb-modobj-grothendieck], [def-sfb-modobj-internal-hom], [lem-sfb-modobj-flat-resolutions], under the ambient hypotheses with which [sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars] defines $T_W$; Res is exact and Ext is exact (step 2), so Ext preserves quasi-isomorphisms between K-flat complexes. Hence $\psi_{QP}$ is invertible for K-flat $P$. Every complex has a K-flat resolution [lem-sfb-abstract-kflat-resolution], so $\psi$ is a natural isomorphism; with it, $\eta^W$ is the localized termwise unit $m\mapsto1\otimes m$.

The underived comparison [def-sfb-comap-lower-star-iso] identifies the same underlying pushforward, and [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback] specifies its scalar action through $\eta_f$. Thus multiplication by $b_i^Y$ on $f_*^F N$ is $f_*^F$ of multiplication by $b_i^X$ on $N$, because these basis sections correspond under inverse image by step 1. For a complex representing $N$, choose an $F_X$-module K-injective resolution $N\to I$. By [lem-sfb-comap-preserves-k-injectives], applicable by the flatness in step 2 at every scheme, $\operatorname{Res}I$ is K-injective over $E_X$. Thus the two sides of the derived comparison [def-sfb-derived-comap-lower-star-iso] are computed on $I$ and $\operatorname{Res}I$ by [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. On these models $e$ is the localization of the underived identity comparison in each degree. Multiplication by $b_i$ is a chain map, so the same scalar-action equality holds through $e$. Naturality of $e$ for this multiplication and $F_Y$-linearity of $c_K$ let us multiply the equality of step 5 by $b_i$. Since $j_i^W=b_i^W\eta^W$, we obtain
$$e_{T_XK}\,U_Y(c_K)\,j_i^Y(GK)=G(j_i^X(K))\qquad(1\leq i\leq d).$$
Under the coordinates of step 2 these are exactly the $d$ injections defining $a_K$ in step 3. Equality on the injections determines a morphism out of a finite biproduct, so the restricted (Push), followed by $e$, is that canonical finite-sum map.

The coordinate identifications and $e$ are isomorphisms, and $a_K$ is an isomorphism by step 3. Step 6 therefore makes $U_Y(c_K)$ invertible. Step 4 makes $c_K$ invertible. This applies to every unbounded $K$. The inverses form a natural transformation: the naturality equation for $c$ can be multiplied on either side by its component inverses. Hence (Push) is an isomorphism of functors as asserted.

split_report.summary: Preserved the statement and expanded its finite-basis proof into seven steps. Reused existing basis, scalar-coordinate, exact-derived and cohomology-detection nodes. Verified the particular mate by its unit equation and multiplication by each compatible basis section; no new nodes or Lean attachments. Reviewer FIX (2026-10-21): step 5 now proves that the derived scalar-extension unit is the localized termwise unit via lem-sfb-exact-right-adjoint-kflat-representative and K-flat resolutions; step 2 uses that identification.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the finite-extension (Push) clause in step 1 of sk-prop-sfb-finite-extension-compatibility and all sentences of lem-sfb-subfield-push-iso.proof.md: compatible bases (step 1), derived coordinates (step 2), finite sums (step 3), conservativity (step 4), and identification of the specified comparison (steps 5-7).

tool_uses.why: Provides an integral basis for the coefficient fields; the finite-extension compatibility unit uses this generic coefficient algebra without restating it.
Provides the actual finite-free bases on arbitrary schemes and their inverse-image compatibility, required by the unit's finite-sum route.
Supplies exact extension of scalars on every scheme, as required by the unit's flatness clause.
Provides the coordinate maps for scalar extension by a finite free internal ring module, a generic tensor calculation used in the prescribed finite-sum proof.
Identifies the termwise derived composite of two exact functors; it does not use the finite-extension compatibility conclusion.

Generic adjunction calculus (Stacks 06YY): identifies the unit of the derived scalar adjunction with the localized termwise unit for exact extension; no node of the unit's route states this, and it does not replace any step of the unit.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q33-73abb3951 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read in full: the item, all 20 cited statements, the main-20261015 item, proof and unit texts, the route closure and the tool uses. The statement matches the blueprint verbatim and is not weakened. The seven steps follow the blueprint's finite-basis route: basis, coordinates, finite products via the right adjoint Rf_*, conservativity of exact restriction, the mate unit equation, the action of the basis elements b_i, and assembly. The mate calculation and the b_i equations check out. There are no new nodes and no cycles. The declared tool uses (integral basis, cartesian finite-free, subfield-flat, finite-free scalar coordinates, exact-derived composition) are accepted. One fault, C1/C4: step 5 asserted without citation that the unit of the specified derived adjunction T_W ⊣ D(Res) is the localized termwise unit m ↦ 1⊗m. No cited node states this; the exact-functor identification of step 2 is arbitrary, and step 6's j_i = b_i·η depends on it. Fixed in step 5: ψ, the transpose of the localized unit, is invertible by lem-sfb-exact-right-adjoint-kflat-representative (Stacks 06YY), whose hypotheses for Mod_{E_W} come from lem-sfb-modobj-grothendieck, def-sfb-modobj-internal-hom and lem-sfb-modobj-flat-resolutions. It extends to every object by lem-sfb-abstract-kflat-resolution. Step 2 now uses ψ as its identification, and the lemma is added to split_report.tool_uses.
